purpose: Explicit source-file classification for first-party chat and AI caller drift review. Classification describes the observed source path and does not grant provider eligibility or authorization.

scanner.contract: Inventory every production source file in api/cli scope matching any configured regex. Broad gateway-import, CLI-name, and endpoint patterns intentionally surface adapters, policy/configuration, health probes, embeddings, media, and false-positive business endpoints; retain these with infrastructure or the actual observed class rather than silently dropping them. Compare paths, not match counts. New paths must be classified; disappeared paths require deliberate review. This is not semantic completeness for every SDK or dynamically assembled caller.

known_gaps: R24-feature-prompt-ownership.md says 13 chat.default scenarios were not semantically surveyed. The broadened scan catches role labels, common generated gateway imports, Connect service names, common provider endpoints, and resource CLI references, but cannot prove completeness for all SDKs, dynamically assembled URLs, generated clients, or other commands.

Broad patterns intentionally retain false positives and support files, tagged infrastructure. A file-level class describes its associated path or matched behavior; mixed provider files may contain multiple selectable sources.

Agent Manager structuredresult is advisory typed extraction of domain run output. Its source explicitly says it does not resolve a coding-agent role or start a runner; it uses generic typed inference without a pinned feature contract, so class is in_app.

Document Manager applies privacy-dependent routing ceilings, but privacy-sensitive/local-first is not necessarily LOCAL_ONLY. Its unpinned model use is in_app; request builders and privacy policies are infrastructure.
Device Studio geometry has worker-integrity, schema, provider-call and spend bounds, but the matched callsite does not verify a published instruction digest; it stays in_app.
Media generation entries are separate from chat. They are classified bounded_feature under R24 media output/operation limits and execution accounting, without claiming a pinned text instruction.
